newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU keeps up human rights pressure on Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: EU keeps up human rights pressure on Nigeria.

text.p: The European Union on Monday extended for a further six months restrictions on contact with Nigerian officials, saying not enough progress had been made in ending human rights abuses.
In a statement, the foreign ministers of the 15-nation bloc said it remained "profoundly concerned" about the human rights situation in Nigeria despite certain positive signs from the government.

"Whilst it has noted a number of positive developments, particularly the pivotal role played by Nigeria in promoting the peace process in Liberia, the EU does not consider that sufficient progress has been made to warrant the removal of existing measures at this time," the statement said.
It made no mention of Sierra Leone, where Nigerian troops have been sent to oust the perpetrators of a military coup.
The EU imposed a series of punitive measures on Nigeria at the end of 1995 following the execution of author Ken Saro Wiwa and eight other rights activists.
Among the measures were restrictions on arms sales, visas, development cooperation, military attaches and sports contacts.
